legein = speaking-out; logos = the prevailing that has been spoken out / become manifest.

kryptein (Verbergen) = keeping in concealment; established as the opposite of legein from Heraclitus Frgm. 93 (the Oracle gives a sign).
legein (revealing) and kryptein (concealing) are explicit opposites; the logos wrests the prevailing from concealment.

Aristotle's physiologoi are not 'physiologists'/'philosophers of nature' but the primordial title for those who question beings as a whole and bring physis to revealedness.
First meaning of physis: a regional concept, the physei onta (self-prevailing) opposed to the techne onta (the produced).
Second meaning of physis: prevailing-as-such, the inner essence/law of any matter — in Aristotle, ousia, the being of beings.
That which makes beings beings (ousia, still called physis by Aristotle) is the second object of First Philosophy.
Aristotle amalgamates the dual orientation — beings as a whole AND the being (ousia) of beings — as prote philosophia / philosophizing proper.
Aristotle 'says nothing' about how the two orientations form a unity; the question is open 'to this day' and 'is not even posed any more today'.

epistasthai = to stand before a matter and know one's way around in it; only in Aristotle does episteme take the decided sense of 'science'.
physis, ethos (ethics) and the logos itself are codified as logic/physics/ethics — the decline of philosophizing proper, in which 'living questioning dies out'.

First Philosophy fit no discipline ('embarrassment'); filed positionally 'behind physics' — a technical title saying nothing about content.
meta = after/behind/post (cf. methodos), purely positional; indicates only the order of the writings.
meta shifts via metabole (changeover, Umschlag) to over/beyond (trans): metaphysics = knowledge of the suprasensuous, conceived in terms of content.
